newsitem.title: USA: Colonial Pipeline shifts calendar to skip cycle.
newsitem.headline: Colonial Pipeline shifts calendar to skip cycle.

text.p: The Colonial Pipeline will shift its scheduling calendar to eliminate a distillate cycle in mid-February to make up for the 10-day scheduling delay from 1996.

The Houston-to-New York pipeline will skip the fifth cycle, passing directly from the fourth to sixth cycle in mid-February, though no disruptions to supplies will occur. Each calendar year is made up of 36 ten-day pipeline cycles.
"The time we lost to the leak in late June and the pressure restrictions in the fall prevented us from keeping on schedule," according to company source.

Heavy demand in the U.S. Northeast for distillates, which include heating oil, diesel and jet fuel, kept the space on the line at a premium. The pipeline was shut briefly in June after a rupture in South Carolina.

The arterial Colonial Pipeline extends from Houston to Linden, New Jersey, on the edge of New York Harbor and includes an 888,000 barrel per day (bpd) distillate line and a 1.2 million bpd gasoline line.
The pipeline extended space allocations through January because of heavy shipping demand. The allocations could be extended into February, pipeline officials said.
